summary: Arrival at the Holloway parlor and initial observation of room features (mantel, mirror, windows); quick sketching of measurements on an envelope.
Loosened mirror from its mounting and found a diary folded flat against the wall behind it.
Opened the diary and read notes about light angles and lamps; excerpt noted: 'Measure the angle at noon; do not trust the hour by the clock.'
Found a loose floorboard two feet east of the hearth, pried it up, and recovered a small brass key from beneath it.
Performed an informal test by moving a hand near the mirror and observed a fractional lag in the mirror's reflection.
Felt a faint, regular tapping through the plaster (one-two, pause, one-two) and noted the rhythmic modulation under the palm.
Recorded measurements on the envelope and resolved to undertake controlled optical tests (lamp angles, precise measures) to reproduce the observed lag.

Visited the town archive; Mr. Calder produced a brittle clipping: Holloway Gazette photograph dated March 14, 1972 (Box 4, Folder 12, Accession HA-1972-03). The clipping shows mantel, mirror seam, and east windows.
Spoke with Mrs. Haverford, who recounted neighborhood memory and warned: 'Mind the seam, love — and don't light it at noon.'
Returned to the parlor, spread the diary on the mantel, and read dated entries including 1972-03-09 and 1972-03-21. Verbatim entries added to diary notes.

Formed a working hypothesis: the seam in the mirror's silvering may channel an aligned ray and activate the mirror's anomalous reflection behaviour; wrote two falsifiable predictions (reproduce angle; interrupt reflective path).
Measured and pencilled setup on the envelope: lamp six feet from the mantel, flame ~18 inches above the hearth, aligned seven inches left of mirror centre; protractor ready and oil lamp ordered.
Executed controlled lamp test: lamp set per pencilled marks; flame lit; seam shimmered and reflection lag observed; mirror displayed impossible reflected geometry and bluish light.

Used brass key to unlock attic hatch, climbed into attic, and observed a split slat on the north rafter admitting a shaft of lamp-light aimed back toward the mantel; slat gap ~2 in, 2 ft from hatch, 10 ft from east window.

Observed reflected apparition: Hannah tapped the inside of the mirror frame in counts and mouthed a word ('light'); the reflected figure matched Lena's fingertip movement and revealed the word 'free' in the reflected dust while the real dust remained unmoved.
Read the diary's March 24, 1972 ritual directives aloud and performed the measured ritual: marked seam, placed flame at pencilled spot, spoke Hannah Hale's name and the diary line as instructed.

Under symmetric alignment of lamp and attic-slat beam across the mirror seam (lamp 6 ft from mantel; flame 18 in above hearth; aligned 7 in left of mirror centre; attic-slat beam intersecting), the seam acted as a midplane conduit and effected an exchange: Lena displaced into the mirror-reflected space (loc-parlor-reflection) while Hannah occupied Lena's body in the house. Lena reports confinement behind the glass and observes Hannah leaving in her body.
